──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n287\t// Percentile helpers\n288\t// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n289\t\n290\t/// Calculate the 95th percentile from a slice of values.\n291\t///\n292\t/// The 95th percentile (p95) is the value below which 95% of observations\n293\t/// fall. It is commonly used to understand the \"tail\" of a distribution\n294\t/// — for example, in latency metrics, p95 tells you that 95% of requests\n295\t/// completed within this time, while the slowest 5% took longer.\n296\t///\n297\t/// # Edge Cases\n298\t///\n299\t/// This function handles all edge cases gracefully:\n300\t///\n301\t/// - **Empty slice**: Returns `0` (no data available)\n302\t/// - **Single element**: Returns that element (the only value available)\n303\t/// - **Two elements**: Uses linear interpolation to estimate p95 between the two values\n304\t/// - **Small samples (2-3 elements)**: Linear interpolation provides a reasonable estimate\n305\t///\n306\t/// All edge cases return sensible results without panicking.\n307\t///\n308\t/// # Algorithm\n309\t///\n310\t/// This function uses **linear interpolation**, which is the same method\n311\t/// used by Criterion.rs and is more accurate than the nearest-rank method:\n312\t///\n313\t/// 1. If the slice is empty, return 0 (no data case)\n314\t/// 2. If the slice has one element, return that element\n315\t/// 3. Sort the values in ascending order\n316\t/// 4. Calculate the rank: `rank = 0.95 * (n - 1)` where `n` is the number of elements\n317\t/// 5. Split the rank into integer and fractional parts\n318\t/// 6. Return the linear interpolation: `floor_value + (ceiling_value - floor_value) * fraction`\n319\t/// 7. Round to the nearest integer for the final result\n320\t///\n321\t/// This method was chosen because:\n322\t/// - **Accurate**: Uses linear interpolation like Criterion.rs for smooth percentile estimates\n323\t/// - **Standard**: Matches the behavior of common benchmarking libraries\n324\t/// - **Well-documented**: The algorithm is described in statistical literature\n325\t/// - **Deterministic**: Always produces the same result for the same input\n326\t/// - **Handles all sample sizes**: Works correctly from 0 to very large datasets\n327\t///\n328\t/// Note: This uses linear interpolation, not nearest-rank. For example, with 10 elements\n329\t/// `[10, 20, ..., 100]`, the 95th percentile is approximately `95.5` (rounded to `96`),\n330\t/// not the maximum value `100`.\n331\t///\n332\t/// # Examples\n333\t///\n334\t/// ## Basic usage with sorted data\n335\t///\n336\t/// ```\n337\t/// use needle::stats::calculate_p95;\n338\t///\n339\t/// let latencies = vec![10u128, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90, 100];\n340\t/// let p95 = calculate_p95(&latencies);\n341\t/// // rank = 0.95 * 9 = 8.55, floor_index = 8, fraction = 0.55\n342\t/// // floor_value = 90, ceiling_value = 100\n343\t/// // interpolated = 90 + 10 * 0.55 = 95.5 → 96\n344\t/// assert_eq!(p95, 96);\n345\t/// ```\n346\t///\n347\t/// ## Works with unsorted input (sorts internally)\n348\t///\n349\t/// ```\n350\t/// use needle::stats::calculate_p95;\n351\t///\n352\t/// let unsorted = vec![100u128, 10, 50, 30, 70, 40, 60, 20, 80, 90];\n353\t/// let p95 = calculate_p95(&unsorted);\n354\t/// assert_eq!(p95, 96); // Function sorts internally → same result\n355\t/// ```\n356\t///\n357\t/// ## Larger dataset\n358\t///\n359\t/// ```\n360\t/// use needle::stats::calculate_p95;\n361\t///\n362\t/// // 20 elements: rank = 0.95 * 19 = 18.05, floor_index = 18, fraction = 0.05\n363\t/// let data = vec![10u128, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90, 100,\n364\t///                  110, 120, 130, 140, 150, 160, 170, 180, 190, 200];\n365\t/// let p95 = calculate_p95(&data);\n366\t/// // floor_value = 190, ceiling_value = 200\n367\t/// // interpolated = 190 + 10 * 0.05 = 190.5 → 191\n368\t/// assert_eq!(p95, 191);\n369\t/// ```\n370\t///\n371\t/// ## Single element (degenerate case)\n372\t///\n373\t/// ```\n374\t/// use needle::stats::calculate_p95;\n375\t///\n376\t/// let single = vec![42u128];\n377\t/// let p95 = calculate_p95(&single);\n378\t/// assert_eq!(p95, 42); // Only value available\n379\t/// ```\n380\t///\n381\t/// ## Empty input\n382\t///\n383\t/// ```\n384\t/// use needle::stats::calculate_p95;\n385\t///\n386\t/// let empty: Vec<u128> = vec![];\n387\t/// let p95 = calculate_p95(&empty);\n388\t/// assert_eq!(p95, 0); // No data → returns 0\n389\t/// ```\n390\t///\n391\t/// ## Two elements (small sample)\n392\t///\n393\t/// ```\n394\t/// use needle::stats::calculate_p95;\n395\t///\n396\t/// let two = vec![10u128, 20];\n397\t/// let p95 = 20\n401\t/// assert_eq!(p95, 20); // Linear interpolation estimates p95\n402\t/// ```\n403\t///\n404\t/// ## Three elements (small sample)\n405\t///\n406\t/// ```\n407\t/// use needle::stats::calculate_p95;\n408\t///\n409\t/// let three = vec![10u128, 20, 30];\n410\t/// let p95 = calculate_p95(&three);\n411\t/// // rank = 0.95 * 2 = 1.9, floor_index = 1, fraction = 0.9\n412\t/// // floor_value = 20, ceiling_value = 30\n413\t/// // interpolated = 20 + 10 * 0.9 = 29.0 → 29\n414\t/// assert_eq!(p95, 29); // Linear interpolation estimates p95\n415\t/// ```\n416\t///\n417\t/// ## Real-world latency example\n418\t///\n419\t/// ```\n420\t/// use needle::stats::calculate_p95;\n421\t///\n422\t/// // Simulated latency data in milliseconds\n423\t/// let 122);\n432\t/// ```\n433\t///\n434\t/// # See Also\n435\t///\n436\t/// - [`docs/p95-calculation-algorithms.md`](../../docs/p95-calculation-algorithms.html) — Comprehensive survey of p95 algorithms and recommendations\n437\tpub fn calculate_p95(latencies: &[u128]) -> u128 {\n438\t    if latencies.is_empty() {\n439\t        return 0;\n440\t    }\n441\t\n442\t    let n = latencies.len();\n443\t    if n == 1 {\n444\t        return latencies[0];\n445\t    }\n446\t\n447\t    let mut sorted = Vec::from(latencies);\n448\t    sorted.sort();\n449\t\n450\t    // Linear interpolation method (like Criterion.rs)\n451\t    // Formula: rank = (p / 100) * (n - 1)\n452\t    // For p95: rank = 0.95 * (n - 1)\n453\t    let rank = 0.95 * (n - 1) as f64;\n454\t    let floor_index = rank.floor() as usize;\n455\t    let fraction = rank - floor_index as f64;\n456\t\n457\t    let floor_value = sorted[floor_index];\n458\t    let ceiling_value = sorted[floor_index + 1];\n459\t\n460\t    // Linear interpolation: floor + (ceiling - floor) * fraction\n461\t    let interpolated = floor_value as f64 + (ceiling_value - floor_value) as f64 * fraction;\n462\t\n463\t    // Round to nearest integer.\n464\t    // Add a small epsilon to handle floating point precision issues (e.g., 95.5 → 95.4999... → 95).\n465\t    // Standard rounding: 95.0-95.499... → 95, 95.5-96.499... → 96\n466\t    let epsilon = 1e-9;\n467\t    (interpolated + epsilon).round() as u128\n468\t}\n469\t\n470\t/// Calculate the 99th percentile from a slice of values.\n471\t///\n472\t/// The 99th percentile (p99) is the value below which 99% of observations\n473\t/// fall. It is commonly used to understand the extreme tail of a distribution\n474\t/// — for example, in latency metrics, p99 tells you that 99% of requests\n475\t/// completed within this time, while the slowest 1% took longer.\n476\t///\n477\t/// # Edge Cases\n478\t///\n479\t/// This function handles all edge cases gracefully:\n480\t///\n481\t/// - **Empty slice**: Returns `0` (no data available)\n482\t/// - **Single element**: Returns that element (the only value available)\n483\t/// - **Two elements**: Uses linear interpolation to estimate p99 between the two values\n484\t/// - **Small samples (2-3 elements)**: Linear interpolation provides a reasonable estimate\n485\t///\n486\t/// All edge cases return sensible results without panicking.\n487\t///\n488\t/// # Algorithm\n489\t///\n490\t/// This function uses **linear interpolation**, which is the same method\n491\t/// used by Criterion.rs and is more accurate than the nearest-rank method:\n492\t///\n493\t/// 1. If the slice is empty, return 0 (no data case)\n494\t/// 2. If the slice has one element, return that element\n495\t/// 3. Sort the values in ascending order\n496\t/// 4. Calculate the rank: `rank = 0.99 * (n - 1)` where `n` is the number of elements\n497\t/// 5. Split the rank into integer and fractional parts\n498\t/// 6. Return the linear interpolation: `floor_value + (ceiling_value - floor_value) * fraction`\n499\t/// 7. Round to the nearest integer for the final result\n500\t///\n501\t/// This method was chosen because:\n502\t/// - **Accurate**: Uses linear interpolation like Criterion.rs for smooth percentile estimates\n503\t/// - **Standard**: Matches the behavior of common benchmarking libraries\n504\t/// - **Well-documented**: The algorithm is described in statistical literature\n505\t/// - **Deterministic**: Always produces the same result for the same input\n506\t/// - **Handles all sample sizes**: Works correctly from 0 to very large datasets\n507\t///\n508\t/// Note: This uses linear interpolation, not nearest-rank. For example, with 10 elements\n509\t/// `[10, 20, ..., 100]`, the 99th percentile is approximately `99.1` (rounded to `99`),\n510\t/// not the maximum value `100`.\n511\t///\n512\t/// # Examples\n513\t///\n514\t/// ## Basic usage with sorted data\n515\t///\n516\t/// ```\n517\t/// use needle::stats::calculate_p99;\n518\t///\n519\t/// let latencies = vec![10u128, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90, 100];\n520\t/// let p99 = calculate_p99(&latencies);\n521\t/// // rank = 0.99 * 9 = 8.91, floor_index = 8, fraction = 0.91\n522\t/// // floor_value = 90, ceiling_value = 100\n523\t/// // interpolated = 90 + 10 * 0.91 = 99.1 → 99\n524\t/// assert_eq!(p99, 99);\n525\t/// ```\n526\t///\n527\t/// ## Works with unsorted input (sorts internally)\n528\t///\n529\t/// ```\n530\t/// use needle::stats::calculate_p99;\n531\t///\n532\t/// let unsorted = vec![100u128, 10, 50, 30, 70, 40, 60, 20, 80, 90];\n533\t/// let p99 = calculate_p99(&unsorted);\n534\t/// assert_eq!(p99, 99); // Function sorts internally → same result\n535\t/// ```\n536\t///\n537\t/// ## Larger dataset\n538\t///\n539\t/// ```\n540\t/// use needle::stats::calculate_p99;\n541\t///\n542\t/// // 20 elements: rank = 0.99 * 19 = 18.81, floor_index = 18, fraction = 0.81\n543\t/// let data = vec![10u128, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90, 100,\n544\t///                  110, 120, 130, 140, 150, 160, 170, 180, 190, 200];\n545\t/// let p99 = calculate_p99(&data);\n546\t/// // floor_value = 190, ceiling_value = 200\n547\t/// // interpolated = 190 + 10 * 0.81 = 198.1 → 198\n548\t/// assert_eq!(p99, 198);\n549\t/// ```\n550\t///\n551\t/// ## Single element (degenerate case)\n552\t///\n553\t/// ```\n554\t/// use needle::stats::calculate_p99;\n555\t///\n556\t/// let single = vec![42u128];\n557\t/// let p99 = calculate_p99(&single);\n558\t/// assert_eq!(p99, 42); // Only value available\n559\t/// ```\n560\t///\n561\t/// ## Empty input\n562\t///\n563\t/// ```\n564\t/// use needle::stats::calculate_p99;\n565\t///\n566\t/// let empty: Vec<u128> = vec![];\n567\t/// let p99 = calculate_p99(&empty);\n568\t/// assert_eq!(p99, 0); // No data → returns 0\n569\t/// ```\n570\t///\n571\t/// ## Two elements (small sample)\n572\t///\n573\t/// ```\n574\t/// use needle::stats::calculate_p99;\n575\t///\n576\t/// let two = vec![10u128, 20];\n577\t/// let p99 = calculate_p99(&two);\n578\t/// // rank = 0.99 * 1 = 0.99, floor_index = 0, fraction = 0.99\n579\t/// // floor_value = 10, ceiling_value = 20\n580\t/// // interpolated = 10 + 10 * 0.99 = 19.9 → 20\n581\t/// assert_eq!(p99, 20); // Linear interpolation estimates p99\n582\t/// ```\n583\t///\n584\t/// ## Three elements (small sample)\n585\t///\n586\t/// ```\n587\t/// use needle::stats::calculate_p99;\n588\t///\n589\t/// let three = vec![10u128, 20, 30];\n590\t/// let p99 = calculate_p99(&three);\n591\t/// // rank = 0.99 * 2 = 1.98, floor_index = 1, fraction = 0.98\n592\t/// // floor_value = 20, ceiling_value = 30\n593\t/// // interpolated = 20 + 10 * 0.98 = 29.8 → 30\n594\t/// assert_eq!(p99, 30); // Linear interpolation estimates p99\n595\t/// ```\n596\t///\n597\t/// ## Real-world latency example\n598\t///\n599\t/// ```\n600\t/// use needle::stats::calculate_p99;\n601\t///\n602\t/// // Simulated latency data in milliseconds\n603\t/// let latencies = vec![\n604\t///     12, 15, 18, 20, 22, 25, 28, 30, 35, 40,\n605\t///     45, 50, 55, 60, 70, 80, 90, 100, 120, 150\n606\t/// ];\n607\t/// let p99 = calculate_p99(&latencies);\n608\t/// // rank = 0.99 * 19 = 18.81, floor_index = 18, fraction = 0.81\n609\t/// // floor_value = 120, ceiling_value = 150\n610\t/// // interpolated = 120 + 30 * 0.81 = 144.3 → 144\n611\t/// assert_eq!(p99, 144);\n612\t/// ```\n613\t///\n614\t/// # See Also\n615\t///\n616\t/// - [`calculate_p95`](fn@calculate_p95) — Calculate the 95th percentile\n617\tpub fn calculate_p99(latencies: &[u128]) -> u128 {\n618\t    if latencies.is_empty() {\n619\t        return 0;\n620\t    }\n621\t\n622\t    let n = latencies.len();\n623\t    if n == 1 {\n624\t        return latencies[0];\n625\t    }\n626\t\n627\t    let mut sorted = Vec::from(latencies);\n628\t    sorted.sort();\n629\t\n630\t    // Linear interpolation method (like Criterion.rs)\n631\t    // Formula: rank = (p / 100) * (n - 1)\n632\t    // For p99: rank = 0.99 * (n - 1)\n633\t    let rank = 0.99 * (n - 1) as f64;\n634\t    let floor_index = rank.floor() as usize;\n635\t    let fraction = rank - floor_index as f64;\n636\t\n637\t    let floor_value = sorted[floor_index];\n638\t    let ceiling_value = sorted[floor_index + 1];\n639\t\n640\t    // Linear interpolation: floor + (ceiling - floor) * fraction\n641\t    let interpolated = floor_value as f64 + (ceiling_value - floor_value) as f64 * fraction;\n642\t\n643\t    // Round to nearest integer.\n644\t    // Add a small epsilon to handle floating point precision issues (e.g., 99.5 → 99.4999... → 99).\n645\t    // Standard rounding: 99.0-99.499... → 99, 99.5-100.499... → 100\n646\t    let epsilon = 1e-9;\n647\t    (interpolated + epsilon).round() as u128\n648\t}\n649\t\n650\t// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n651\t// P95 aggregation utilities\n652\t// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n653\t\n654\t/// Collector for aggregating samples across multiple benchmark iterations.\n655\t///\n656\t/// This struct provides a statistically sound way to aggregate latency measurements\n657\t/// across multiple iterations and calculate a single p95 percentile.\n658\t///\n659\t/// # Statistical Approach\n660\t///\n661\t/// The correct way to aggregate percentiles across multiple iterations is to:\n662\t/// 1. **Pool all samples** from all iterations into a single dataset\n663\t/// 2. **Calculate one p95** on the pooled data\n664\t///\n665\t/// **Do NOT average p95 values** from individual iterations — this is statistically\n666\t/// invalid because percentiles are non-linear statistics. Averaging them produces\n667\t/// misleading results.\n668\t///\n669\t/// # Example\n670\t///\n671\t/// ```no_run\n672\t/// use needle::stats::P95Collector;\n673\t/// use std::time::Instant;\n674\t///\n675\t/// let mut collector = P95Collector::new();\n676\t///\n677\t/// // Run benchmark for 50 iterations\n678\t/// for _ in 0..50 {\n679\t///     let start = Instant::now();\n680\t///     // ... perform work ...\n681\t///     collector.record(start.elapsed().as_micros());\n682\t/// }\n683\t///\n684\t/// // Calculate p95 across all iterations\n685\t/// let p95_us = collector.p95();\n686\t/// println!(\"p95 latency: {} μs\", p95_us);\n687\t/// ```\n688\t#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]\n689\tpub struct P95Collector {\n690\t    /// All recorded latency samples in microseconds.\n691\t    samples: Vec<u128>,\n692\t}\n693\t\n694\timpl P95Collector {\n695\t    /// Create a new empty collector.\n696\t    pub fn new() -> Self {\n697\t        Self {\n698\t            samples: Vec::new(),\n699\t        }\n700\t    }\n701\t\n702\t    /// Create a new collector with pre-allocated capacity.\n703\t    ///\n704\t    /// Use this when you know how many samples you'll collect to avoid\n705\t    /// reallocations during benchmarking.\n706\t    pub fn with_capacity(capacity: usize) -> Self {\n707\t        Self {\n708\t            samples: Vec::with_capacity(capacity),\n709\t        }\n710\t    }\n711\t\n712\t    /// Record a single latency sample in microseconds.\n713\t    pub fn record(&mut self, latency_us: u128) {\n714\t        self.samples.push(latency_us);\n715\t    }\n716\t\n717\t    /// Record multiple latency samples at once.\n718\t    pub fn record_all(&mut self, latencies: impl IntoIterator<Item = u128>) {\n719\t        self.samples.extend(latencies);\n720\t    }\n721\t\n722\t    /// Calculate the p95 percentile across all recorded samples.\n723\t    ///\n724\t    /// Returns `0` if no samples have been recorded.\n725\t    pub fn p95(&self) -> u128 {\n726\t        calculate_p95(&self.samples)\n727\t    }\n728\t\n729\t    /// Return the number of samples collected.\n730\t    pub fn count(&self) -> self.samples.is_empty() {\n749\t            return None;\n750\t        }\n751\t        let min = *self.samples.iter().min().unwrap();\n752\t        let max = *self.samples.iter().max().unwrap();\n753\t        let sum: u128 = self.samples.iter().sum();\n754\t        let avg = sum as f64 / self.samples.len() as f64;\n755\t        Some((min, max, avg))\n756\t    }\n757\t}\n758\t\n759\t// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n760\t// Stats engine — multi-dimensional outcome aggregation\n761\t// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n1466\t\n1467\t    /// Collector for aggregating samples across multiple benchmark iterations.\n1468\t    ///\n1469\t    /// This struct provides a statistically sound way to aggregate latency measurements\n1470\t    /// across multiple iterations and calculate a single p99 percentile.\n1471\t    ///\n1472\t    /// # Statistical Approach\n1473\t    ///\n1474\t    /// The correct way to aggregate percentiles across multiple iterations is to:\n1475\t    /// 1. **Pool all samples** from all iterations into a single dataset\n1476\t    /// 2. **Calculate one p99** on the pooled data\n1477\t    ///\n1478\t    /// **Do NOT average p99 values** from individual iterations — this is statistically\n1479\t    /// invalid because percentiles are non-linear statistics. Averaging them produces\n1480\t    /// misleading results.\n1481\t    ///\n1482\t    /// # Example\n1483\t    ///\n1484\t    /// ```no_run\n1485\t    /// use needle::stats::P99Collector;\n1486\t    /// use std::time::Instant;\n1487\t    ///\n1488\t    /// let mut collector = P99Collector::new();\n1489\t    ///\n1490\t    /// // Run benchmark for 50 iterations\n1491\t    /// for _ in 0..50 {\n1492\t    ///     let start = Instant::now();\n1493\t    ///     // ... perform work ...\n1494\t    ///     collector.record(start.elapsed().as_micros());\n1495\t    /// }\n1496\t    ///\n1497\t    /// // Calculate p99 across all iterations\n1498\t    /// let p99_us = collector.p99();\n1499\t    /// println!(\"p99 latency: {} μs\", p99_us);\n1500\t    /// ```\n1501\t    #[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]\n1502\t    pub struct P99Collector {\n1503\t        /// All recorded latency samples in microseconds.\n1504\t        samples: Vec<u128>,\n1505\t    }\n1506\t\n1507\t    impl P99Collector {\n1508\t        /// Create a new empty collector.\n1509\t        pub fn new() -> Self {\n1510\t            Self {\n1511\t                samples: Vec::new(),\n1512\t            }\n1513\t        }\n1514\t\n1515\t        /// Create a new collector with pre-allocated capacity.\n1516\t        ///\n1517\t        /// Use this when you know how many samples you'll collect to avoid\n1518\t        /// reallocations during benchmarking.\n1519\t        pub fn with_capacity(capacity: usize) -> Self {\n1520\t            Self {\n1521\t                samples: Vec::with_capacity(capacity),\n1522\t            }\n1523\t        }\n1524\t\n1525\t        /// Record a single latency sample in microseconds.\n1526\t        pub fn record(&mut self, latency_us: u128) {\n1527\t ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Percentile helpers\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Calculate the 95th percentile from a slice of values.\n///\n/// The 95th percentile (p95) is the value below which 95% of observations\n/// fall. It is commonly used to understand the \"tail\" of a distribution\n/// — for example, in latency metrics, p95 tells you that 95% of requests\n/// completed within this time, while the slowest 5% took longer.\n///\n/// # Edge Cases\n///\n/// This function handles all edge cases gracefully:\n///\n/// - **Empty slice**: Returns `0` (no data available)\n/// - **Single element**: Returns that element (the only value available)\n/// - **Two elements**: Uses linear interpolation to estimate p95 between the two values\n/// - **Small samples (2-3 elements)**: Linear interpolation provides a reasonable estimate\n///\n/// All edge cases return sensible results without panicking.\n///\n/// # Algorithm\n///\n/// This function uses **linear interpolation**, which is the same method\n/// used by Criterion.rs and is more accurate than the nearest-rank method:\n///\n/// 1. If the slice is empty, return 0 (no data case)\n/// 2. If the slice has one element, return that element\n/// 3. Sort the values in ascending order\n/// 4. Calculate the rank: `rank = 0.95 * (n - 1)` where `n` is the number of elements\n/// 5. Split the rank into integer and fractional parts\n/// 6. Return the linear interpolation: `floor_value + (ceiling_value - floor_value) * fraction`\n/// 7. Round to the nearest integer for the final result\n///\n/// This method was chosen because:\n/// - **Accurate**: Uses linear interpolation like Criterion.rs for smooth percentile estimates\n/// - **Standard**: Matches the behavior of common benchmarking libraries\n/// - **Well-documented**: The algorithm is described in statistical literature\n/// - **Deterministic**: Always produces the same result for the same input\n/// - **Handles all sample sizes**: Works correctly from 0 to very large datasets\n///\n/// Note: This uses linear interpolation, not nearest-rank. For example, with 10 elements\n/// `[10, 20, ..., 100]`, the 95th percentile is approximately `95.5` (rounded to `96`),\n/// not the maximum value `100`.\n///\n/// # Examples\n///\n/// ## Basic usage with sorted data\n///\n/// ```\n/// use needle::stats::calculate_p95;\n///\n/// let latencies = vec![10u128, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90, 100];\n/// let p95 = calculate_p95(&latencies);\n/// // rank = 0.95 * 9 = 8.55, floor_index = 8, fraction = 0.55\n/// // floor_value = 90, ceiling_value = 100\n/// // interpolated = 90 + 10 * 0.55 = 95.5 → 96\n/// assert_eq!(p95, 96);\n/// ```\n///\n/// ## Works with unsorted input (sorts internally)\n///\n/// ```\n/// use needle::stats::calculate_p95;\n///\n/// let unsorted = vec![100u128, 10, 50, 30, 70, 40, 60, 20, 80, 90];\n/// let p95 = calculate_p95(&unsorted);\n/// assert_eq!(p95, 96); // Function sorts internally → same result\n/// ```\n///\n/// ## Larger dataset\n///\n/// ```\n/// use needle::stats::calculate_p95;\n///\n/// // 20 elements: rank = 0.95 * 19 = 18.05, floor_index = 18, fraction = 0.05\n/// let data = vec![10u128, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90, 100,\n///                  110, 120, 130, 140, 150, 160, 170, 180, 190, 200];\n/// let p95 = calculate_p95(&data);\n/// // floor_value = 190, ceiling_value = 200\n/// // interpolated = 190 + 10 * 0.05 = 190.5 → 191\n/// assert_eq!(p95, 191);\n/// ```\n///\n/// ## Single element (degenerate case)\n///\n/// ```\n/// use needle::stats::calculate_p95;\n///\n/// let single = vec![42u128];\n/// let p95 = calculate_p95(&single);\n/// assert_eq!(p95, 42); // Only value available\n/// ```\n///\n/// ## Empty input\n///\n/// ```\n/// use needle::stats::calculate_p95;\n///\n/// let empty: Vec<u128> = vec![];\n/// let p95 = calculate_p95(&empty);\n/// assert_eq!(p95, 0); // No data → returns 0\n/// ```\n///\n/// ## Two elements (small sample)\n///\n/// ```\n/// use needle::stats::calculate_p95;\n///\n/// let two = vec![10u128, 20];\n/// let p95 = calculate_p95(&two);\n/// // rank = 0.95 * 1 = 0.95, floor_index = 0, fraction = 0.95\n/// // floor_value = 10, ceiling_value = 20\n/// // interpolated = 10 + 10 * 0.95 = 19.5 → 20\n/// assert_eq!(p95, 20); // Linear interpolation estimates p95\n/// ```\n///\n/// ## Three elements (small sample)\n///\n/// ```\n/// use needle::stats::calculate_p95;\n///\n/// let three = vec![10u128, 20, 30];\n/// let p95 = calculate_p95(&three);\n/// // rank = 0.95 * 2 = 1.9, floor_index = 1, fraction = 0.9\n/// // floor_value = 20, ceiling_value = 30\n/// // interpolated = 20 + 10 * 0.9 = 29.0 → 29\n/// assert_eq!(p95, 29); // Linear interpolation estimates p95\n/// ```\n///\n/// ## Real-world latency example\n///\n/// ```\n/// use needle::stats::calculate_p95;\n///\n/// // Simulated latency data in milliseconds\n/// let latencies = vec![\n///     12, 15, 18, 20, 22, 25, 28, 30, 35, 40,\n///     45, 50, 55, 60, 70, 80, 90, 100, 120, 150\n/// ];\n/// let p95 = calculate_p95(&latencies);\n/// // rank = 0.95 * 19 = 18.05, floor_index = 18, fraction = 0.05\n/// // floor_value = 120, ceiling_value = 150\n/// // interpolated = 120 + 30 * 0.05 = 121.5 → 122\n/// assert_eq!(p95, 122);\n/// ```\n///\n/// # See Also\n///\n/// - [`docs/p95-calculation-algorithms.md`](../../docs/p95-calculation-algorithms.html) — Comprehensive survey of p95 algorithms and recommendations\npub fn calculate_p95(latencies: &[u128]) -> u128 {\n    if latencies.is_empty() {\n        return 0;\n    }\n\n    let n = latencies.len();\n    if n == 1 {\n        return latencies[0];\n    }\n\n    let mut sorted = Vec::from(latencies);\n    sorted.sort();\n\n    // Linear interpolation method (like Criterion.rs)\n    // Formula: rank = (p / 100) * (n - 1)\n    // For p95: rank = 0.95 * (n - 1)\n    let rank = 0.95 * (n - 1) as f64;\n    let floor_index = rank.floor() as usize;\n    let fraction = rank - floor_index as f64;\n\n    let floor_value = sorted[floor_index];\n    let ceiling_value = sorted[floor_index + 1];\n\n    // Linear interpolation: floor + (ceiling - floor) * fraction\n    let interpolated = floor_value as f64 + (ceiling_value - floor_value) as f64 * fraction;\n\n    // Round to nearest integer.\n    // Add a small epsilon to handle floating point precision issues (e.g., 95.5 → 95.4999... → 95).\n    // Standard rounding: 95.0-95.499... → 95, 95.5-96.499... → 96\n    let epsilon = 1e-9;\n    (interpolated + epsilon).round() as u128\n}\n\n/// Calculate the 99th percentile from a slice of values.\n///\n/// The 99th percentile (p99) is the value below which 99% of observations\n/// fall. It is commonly used to understand the extreme tail of a distribution\n/// — for example, in latency metrics, p99 tells you that 99% of requests\n/// completed within this time, while the slowest 1% took longer.\n///\n/// # Edge Cases\n///\n/// This function handles all edge cases gracefully:\n///\n/// - **Empty slice**: Returns `0` (no data available)\n/// - **Single element**: Returns that element (the only value available)\n/// - **Two elements**: Uses linear interpolation to estimate p99 between the two values\n/// - **Small samples (2-3 elements)**: Linear interpolation provides a reasonable estimate\n///\n/// All edge cases return sensible results without panicking.\n///\n/// # Algorithm\n///\n/// This function uses **linear interpolation**, which is the same method\n/// used by Criterion.rs and is more accurate than the nearest-rank method:\n///\n/// 1. If the slice is empty, return 0 (no data case)\n/// 2. If the slice has one element, return that element\n/// 3. Sort the values in ascending order\n/// 4. Calculate the rank: `rank = 0.99 * (n - 1)` where `n` is the number of elements\n/// 5. Split the rank into integer and fractional parts\n/// 6. Return the linear interpolation: `floor_value + (ceiling_value - floor_value) * fraction`\n/// 7. Round to the nearest integer for the final result\n///\n/// This method was chosen because:\n/// - **Accurate**: Uses linear interpolation like Criterion.rs for smooth percentile estimates\n/// - **Standard**: Matches the behavior of common benchmarking libraries\n/// - **Well-documented**: The algorithm is described in statistical literature\n/// - **Deterministic**: Always produces the same result for the same input\n/// - **Handles all sample sizes**: Works correctly from 0 to very large datasets\n///\n/// Note: This uses linear interpolation, not nearest-rank. For example, with 10 elements\n/// `[10, 20, ..., 100]`, the 99th percentile is approximately `99.1` (rounded to `99`),\n/// not the maximum value `100`.\n///\n/// # Examples\n///\n/// ## Basic usage with sorted data\n///\n/// ```\n/// use needle::stats::calculate_p99;\n///\n/// let latencies = vec![10u128, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90, 100];\n/// let p99 = calculate_p99(&latencies);\n/// // rank = 0.99 * 9 = 8.91, floor_index = 8, fraction = 0.91\n/// // floor_value = 90, ceiling_value = 100\n/// // interpolated = 90 + 10 * 0.91 = 99.1 → 99\n/// assert_eq!(p99, 99);\n/// ```\n///\n/// ## Works with unsorted input (sorts internally)\n///\n/// ```\n/// use needle::stats::calculate_p99;\n///\n/// let unsorted = vec![100u128, 10, 50, 30, 70, 40, 60, 20, 80, 90];\n/// let p99 = calculate_p99(&unsorted);\n/// assert_eq!(p99, 99); // Function sorts internally → same result\n/// ```\n///\n/// ## Larger dataset\n///\n/// ```\n/// use needle::stats::calculate_p99;\n///\n/// // 20 elements: rank = 0.99 * 19 = 18.81, floor_index = 18, fraction = 0.81\n/// let data = vec![10u128, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90, 100,\n///                  110, 120, 130, 140, 150, 160, 170, 180, 190, 200];\n/// let p99 = calculate_p99(&data);\n/// // floor_value = 190, ceiling_value = 200\n/// // interpolated = 190 + 10 * 0.81 = 198.1 → 198\n/// assert_eq!(p99, 198);\n/// ```\n///\n/// ## Single element (degenerate case)\n///\n/// ```\n/// use needle::stats::calculate_p99;\n///\n/// let single = vec![42u128];\n/// let p99 = calculate_p99(&single);\n/// assert_eq!(p99, 42); // Only value available\n/// ```\n///\n/// ## Empty input\n///\n/// ```\n/// use needle::stats::calculate_p99;\n///\n/// let empty: Vec<u128> = vec![];\n/// let p99 = calculate_p99(&empty);\n/// assert_eq!(p99, 0); // No data → returns 0\n/// ```\n///\n/// ## Two elements (small sample)\n///\n/// ```\n/// use needle::stats::calculate_p99;\n///\n/// let two = vec![10u128, 20];\n/// let p99 = calculate_p99(&two);\n/// // rank = 0.99 * 1 = 0.99, floor_index = 0, fraction = 0.99\n/// // floor_value = 10, ceiling_value = 20\n/// // interpolated = 10 + 10 * 0.99 = 19.9 → 20\n/// assert_eq!(p99, 20); // Linear interpolation estimates p99\n/// ```\n///\n/// ## Three elements (small sample)\n///\n/// ```\n/// use needle::stats::calculate_p99;\n///\n/// let three = vec![10u128, 20, 30];\n/// let p99 = calculate_p99(&three);\n/// // rank = 0.99 * 2 = 1.98, floor_index = 1, fraction = 0.98\n/// // floor_value = 20, ceiling_value = 30\n/// // interpolated = 20 + 10 * 0.98 = 29.8 → 30\n/// assert_eq!(p99, 30); // Linear interpolation estimates p99\n/// ```\n///\n/// ## Real-world latency example\n///\n/// ```\n/// use needle::stats::calculate_p99;\n///\n/// // Simulated latency data in milliseconds\n/// let latencies = vec![\n///     12, 15, 18, 20, 22, 25, 28, 30, 35, 40,\n///     45, 50, 55, 60, 70, 80, 90, 100, 120, 150\n/// ];\n/// let p99 = calculate_p99(&latencies);\n/// // rank = 0.99 * 19 = 18.81, floor_index = 18, fraction = 0.81\n/// // floor_value = 120, ceiling_value = 150\n/// // interpolated = 120 + 30 * 0.81 = 144.3 → 144\n/// assert_eq!(p99, 144);\n/// ```\n///\n/// # See Also\n///\n/// - [`calculate_p95`](fn@calculate_p95) — Calculate the 95th percentile\npub fn calculate_p99(latencies: &[u128]) -> u128 {\n    if latencies.is_empty() {\n        return 0;\n    }\n\n    let n = latencies.len();\n    if n == 1 {\n        return latencies[0];\n    }\n\n    let mut sorted = Vec::from(latencies);\n    sorted.sort();\n\n    // Linear interpolation method (like Criterion.rs)\n    // Formula: rank = (p / 100) * (n - 1)\n    // For p99: rank = 0.99 * (n - 1)\n    let rank = 0.99 * (n - 1) as f64;\n    let floor_index = rank.floor() as usize;\n    let fraction = rank - floor_index as f64;\n\n    let floor_value = sorted[floor_index];\n    let ceiling_value = sorted[floor_index + 1];\n\n    // Linear interpolation: floor + (ceiling - floor) * fraction\n    let interpolated = floor_value as f64 + (ceiling_value - floor_value) as f64 * fraction;\n\n    // Round to nearest integer.\n    // Add a small epsilon to handle floating point precision issues (e.g., 99.5 → 99.4999... → 99).\n    // Standard rounding: 99.0-99.499... → 99, 99.5-100.499... → 100\n    let epsilon = 1e-9;\n    (interpolated + epsilon).round() as u128\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// P95 aggregation utilities\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Collector for aggregating samples across multiple benchmark iterations.\n///\n/// This struct provides a statistically sound way to aggregate latency measurements\n/// across multiple iterations and calculate a single p95 percentile.\n///\n/// # Statistical Approach\n///\n/// The correct way to aggregate percentiles across multiple iterations is to:\n/// 1. **Pool all samples** from all iterations into a single dataset\n/// 2. **Calculate one p95** on the pooled data\n///\n/// **Do NOT average p95 values** from individual iterations — this is statistically\n/// invalid because percentiles are non-linear statistics. Averaging them produces\n/// misleading results.\n///\n/// # Example\n///\n/// ```no_run\n/// use needle::stats::P95Collector;\n/// use std::time::Instant;\n///\n/// let mut collector = P95Collector::new();\n///\n/// // Run benchmark for 50 iterations\n/// for _ in 0..50 {\n///     let start = Instant::now();\n///     // ... perform work ...\n///     collector.record(start.elapsed().as_micros());\n/// }\n///\n/// // Calculate p95 across all iterations\n/// let p95_us = collector.p95();\n/// println!(\"p95 latency: {} μs\", p95_us);\n/// ```\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]\npub struct P95Collector {\n    /// All recorded latency samples in microseconds.\n    samples: Vec<u128>,\n}\n\nimpl P95Collector {\n    /// Create a new empty collector.\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        Self {\n            samples: Vec::new(),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Create a new collector with pre-allocated capacity.\n    ///\n    /// Use this when you know how many samples you'll collect to avoid\n    /// reallocations during benchmarking.\n    pub fn with_capacity(capacity: usize) -> Self {\n        Self {\n            samples: Vec::with_capacity(capacity),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Record a single latency sample in microseconds.\n    pub fn record(&mut self, latency_us: u128) {\n        self.samples.push(latency_us);\n    }\n\n    /// Record multiple latency samples at once.\n    pub fn record_all(&mut self, latencies: impl IntoIterator<Item = u128>) {\n        self.samples.extend(latencies);\n    }\n\n    /// Calculate the p95 percentile across all recorded samples.\n    ///\n    /// Returns `0` if no samples have been recorded.\n    pub fn p95(&self) -> u128 {\n        calculate_p95(&self.samples)\n    }\n\n    /// Return the number of samples collected.\n    pub fn count(&self) -> usize {\n        self.samples.len()\n    }\n\n    /// Clear all recorded samples.\n    pub fn clear(&mut self) {\n        self.samples.clear();\n    }\n\n    /// Get a reference to the underlying samples.\n    pub fn samples(&self) -> &[u128] {\n        &self.samples\n    }\n\n    /// Calculate additional statistics on the collected samples.\n    ///\n    /// Returns `(min, max, avg)` in microseconds, or `None` if no samples.\n    pub fn stats(&self) -> Option<(u128, u128, f64)> {\n        if self.samples.is_empty() {\n            return None;\n        }\n        let min = *self.samples.iter().min().unwrap();\n        let max = *self.samples.iter().max().unwrap();\n        let sum: u128 = self.samples.iter().sum();\n        let avg = sum as f64 / self.samples.len() as f64;\n        Some((min, max, avg))\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Stats engine — multi-dimensional outcome aggregation\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Grouping dimension for the `needle stats` command.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum StatsDimension {\n    /// Group by template version tag (e.g., `\"pluck-v2\"`).\n    TemplateVersion,\n    /// Group by template name / task type (e.g., `\"pluck\"`).\n    TaskType,\n    /// Group by worker identifier (e.g., `\"needle-alpha\"`).\n    Worker,\n}\n\n/// Aggregated statistics row for one value of a grouping dimension.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq)]\npub struct StatsRow {\n    /// The dimension value (version, task type, or worker id).\n    pub key: String,\n    /// Total number of beads dispatched in this group.\n    pub beads: u64,\n    /// Number of beads that completed with `\"Success\"` outcome.\n    pub pass: u64,\n    /// Number of beads that completed with `\"Failure\"` outcome.\n    pub fail: u64,\n    /// Number of beads that completed with `\"Timeout\"` outcome.\n    pub timeout: u64,\n    /// Sum of (tokens_in + tokens_out) across all effort events in this group.\n    pub total_tokens: u64,\n    /// Sum of `estimated_cost_usd` across all effort events in this group.\n    pub total_cost_usd: f64,\n    /// Number of effort events with token/cost data (denominator for averages).\n    pub effort_events: u64,\n}\n\nimpl StatsRow {\n    /// Pass rate as a fraction in `[0.0, 1.0]`. `None` when `beads == 0`.\n    pub fn pass_rate(&self) -> Option<f64> {\n        if self.beads == 0 {\n            None\n        } else {\n            Some(self.pass as f64 / self.beads as f64)\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Average total tokens (in + out) per effort event. `None` when no effort data.\n    pub fn avg_tokens(&self) -> Option<f64> {\n        if self.effort_events == 0 {\n            None\n        } else {\n            Some(self.total_tokens as f64 / self.effort_events as f64)\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Average cost in USD per effort event. `None` when no effort data.\n    pub fn avg_cost_usd(&self) -> Option<f64> {\n        if self.effort_events == 0 {\n            None\n        } else {\n            Some(self.total_cost_usd / self.effort_events as f64)\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Compute per-group statistics from a pre-filtered slice of telemetry events.\n///\n/// Correlates `agent.dispatched`, `outcome.classified`, and `effort.recorded`\n/// events by `bead_id`, grouping each bead under the chosen `dimension`.\n///\n/// Pass the result of [`telemetry::read_logs`] (already time-filtered) here.\npub fn compute_stats(\n    events: &[crate::telemetry::TelemetryEvent],\n    dimension: StatsDimension,\n) -> Vec<StatsRow> {\n    use std::collections::HashMap;\n\n    // bead_id → dimension key (populated from agent.dispatched events)\n    let mut bead_key: HashMap<String, String> = HashMap::new();\n    let mut rows: BTreeMap<String, StatsRow> = BTreeMap::new();\n\n    for event in events {\n        match event.event_type.as_str() {\n            \"agent.dispatched\" => {\n                let bead_id = match event.bead_id.as_ref() {\n                    Some(b) => b.as_ref().to_string(),\n                    None => continue,\n                };\n                let key = match dimension {\n                    StatsDimension::TemplateVersion => event\n                        .data\n                        .get(\"template_version\")\n                        .and_then(|v| v.as_str())\n                        .unwrap_or(\"unknown\")\n                        .to_string(),\n                    StatsDimension::TaskType => event\n                        .data\n                        .get(\"template_name\")\n                        .and_then(|v| v.as_str())\n                        .unwrap_or(\"unknown\")\n                        .to_string(),\n                    StatsDimension::Worker => event.worker_id.clone(),\n                };\n                bead_key.insert(bead_id, key.clone());\n                let row = rows.entry(key.clone()).or_insert_with(|| StatsRow {\n                    key: key.clone(),\n                    ..Default::default()\n                });\n                row.beads += 1;\n            }\n\n            \"outcome.classified\" => {\n                let bead_id = match event.bead_id.as_ref() {\n                    Some(b) => b.as_ref().to_string(),\n                    None => continue,\n                };\n                if let Some(key) = bead_key.get(&bead_id) {\n                    if let Some(row) = rows.get_mut(key) {\n                        match event.data.get(\"outcome\").and_then(|v| v.as_str()) {\n                            Some(\"Success\") => row.pass += 1,\n                            Some(\"Failure\") => row.fail += 1,\n                            Some(\"Timeout\") => row.timeout += 1,\n                            _ => {}\n                        }\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n\n            \"effort.recorded\" => {\n                let bead_id = match event.bead_id.as_ref() {\n                    Some(b) => b.as_ref().to_string(),\n                    None => continue,\n                };\n                if let Some(key) = bead_key.get(&bead_id) {\n                    if let Some(row) = rows.get_mut(key) {\n                        let tokens_in = event\n                            .data\n                            .get(\"tokens_in\")\n                            .and_then(|v| v.as_u64())\n                            .unwrap_or(0);\n                        let tokens_out = event\n                            .data\n                            .get(\"tokens_out\")\n                            .and_then(|v| v.as_u64())\n                            .unwrap_or(0);\n                        row.total_tokens += tokens_in + tokens_out;\n                        if let Some(cost) = event\n                            .data\n                            .get(\"estimated_cost_usd\")\n                            .and_then(|v| v.as_f64())\n                        {\n                            row.total_cost_usd += cost;\n                        }\n                        row.effort_events += 1;\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n\n            _ => {}\n        }\n    }\n\n    rows.into_values().collect()\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Tests\n// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n    /// Collector for aggregating samples across multiple benchmark iterations.\n    ///\n    /// This struct provides a statistically sound way to aggregate latency measurements\n    /// across multiple iterations and calculate a single p99 percentile.\n    ///\n    /// # Statistical Approach\n    ///\n    /// The correct way to aggregate percentiles across multiple iterations is to:\n    /// 1. **Pool all samples** from all iterations into a single dataset\n    /// 2. **Calculate one p99** on the pooled data\n    ///\n    /// **Do NOT average p99 values** from individual iterations — this is statistically\n    /// invalid because percentiles are non-linear statistics. Averaging them produces\n    /// misleading results.\n    ///\n    /// # Example\n    ///\n    /// ```no_run\n    /// use needle::stats::P99Collector;\n    /// use std::time::Instant;\n    ///\n    /// let mut collector = P99Collector::new();\n    ///\n    /// // Run benchmark for 50 iterations\n    /// for _ in 0..50 {\n    ///     let start = Instant::now();\n    ///     // ... perform work ...\n    ///     collector.record(start.elapsed().as_micros());\n    /// }\n    ///\n    /// // Calculate p99 across all iterations\n    /// let p99_us = collector.p99();\n    /// println!(\"p99 latency: {} μs\", p99_us);\n    /// ```\n    #[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]\n    pub struct P99Collector {\n        /// All recorded latency samples in microseconds.\n        samples: Vec<u128>,\n    }\n\n    impl P99Collector {\n        /// Create a new empty collector.\n        pub fn new() -> Self {\n            Self {\n                samples: Vec::new(),\n            }\n        }\n\n        /// Create a new collector with pre-allocated capacity.\n        ///\n        /// Use this when you know how many samples you'll collect to avoid\n        /// reallocations during benchmarking.\n        pub fn with_capacity(capacity: usize) -> Self {\n            Self {\n                samples: Vec::with_capacity(capacity),\n            }\n        }\n\n        /// Record a single latency sample in microseconds.\n        pub fn record(&mut self, latency_us: u128) {\n            self.samples.push(latency_us);\n        }\n\n        /// Record multiple latency samples at once.\n        pub fn record_all(&mut self, latencies: impl IntoIterator<Item = u128>) {\n            self.samples.extend(latencies);\n        }\n\n        /// Calculate the p99 percentile across all recorded samples.\n        ///\n        /// Returns `0` if no samples have been recorded.\n        pub fn p99(&self) -> u128 {\n            calculate_p99(&self.samples)\n        }\n\n        /// Return the number of samples collected.\n        pub fn count(&self) -> usize {\n            self.samples.len()\n        }\n\n        /// Clear all recorded samples.\n        pub fn clear(&mut self) {\n            self.samples.clear();\n        }\n\n        /// Get a reference to the underlying samples.\n        pub fn samples(&self) -> &[u128] {\n            &self.samples\n        }\n\n        /// Calculate additional statistics on the collected samples.\n        ///\n        /// Returns `(min, max, avg)` in microseconds, or `None` if no samples.\n        pub fn stats(&self) -> Option<(u128, u128, f64)> {\n            if self.samples.is_empty() {\n                return None;\n            }\n            let min = *self.samples.iter().min().unwrap();\n            let max = *self.samples.iter().max().unwrap();\n            let sum: u128 = self.samples.iter().sum();\n            let avg = sum as f64 / self.samples.len() as f64;\n            Some((min, max, avg))\n        }\n    }\n\n    // ── P99Collector tests ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n    #[test]\n    fn p99_collector_empty() {\n        let collector = P99Collector::new();\n
